A shorter version of this note first appeared in the Financial Times . - Where We Are Now I recently spent a month in Asia, including 10 days in China, where I met with senior policy makers in several countries, and I found that over the past few months there has been a big shift in the world order because: 1) The United States’ handling of Iran’s taking of the Strait of Hormuz has led global leaders, especially those in Asia, to conclude that the American public does not have the willingness to endure the discomforts of war and that the US doesn’t have the resources to fight wars on two or more fronts, so it doesn’t have what it takes to fight to maintain its empire. - This situation looks a lot like the British handling of Egypt’s taking of the Suez Canal, which signaled the end of the British Empire. - More specifically, it is now inconceivable that the American public would support an American military response to Chinese pressures a) aimed at Taiwan or b) against countries that are trying to contain China. - This has changed the thinking and actions of leaders in countries that are US allies and that are hosting American bases as a counterweight to China under the assumption that the US will protect them. ## Evidence - items.content_text: # AI Wearables: A Social Challenge, Not an Engineering One. ## Summary By: Nicholas Grous and Varshika Prasanna The promise of AI wearables is perfect information recall paired with an AI agent, representing something substantially different from today’s assistants. Instead of asking AI generic questions, you could interact with an AI agent that knows the surrounding context about you – like history, patterns, and commitments. It could help organize your tasks, remind you of what was said in a meeting, surface commitments you forgot, or help reflect on your behavi… ## Key Claims - By: Nicholas Grous and Varshika Prasanna The promise of AI wearables is perfect information recall paired with an AI agent, representing something substantially different from today’s assistants. - Instead of asking AI generic questions, you could interact with an AI agent that knows the surrounding context about you – like history, patterns, and commitments. - It could help organize your tasks, remind you of what was said in a meeting, surface commitments you forgot, or help reflect on your behaviors. - The value is not just the information, but organized memory and contextual awareness applied to your own life. - Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. ## Evidence - AI wearables are a bet that if AI could see and hear what you do and remember it for you, it would become exponentially more valuable. - The question is not whether AI wearable technology will work. It is whether we are comfortable with a world in which memory is no longer scarce, and forgetting is no longer the default. ## Tensions _None flagged yet._ ## Links - Raw: `kb/inbox/b67a6c016dafd6d9e6f6b29b0cfad4fd43ecbac93c08bdfed8e4edcac0a06970.json` - Concepts: [[concepts/research|Research]] - Overview: [[overview]]

items.content_text: # July 2026 Portfolio Update ## Summary Hey folks. We have just crossed Rebound Capital’s 1st Anniversary , and I want to thank every one of you. The fact that nearly 23,000 of you read my content is a big responsibility. I will keep grinding and doing what I love - finding value in the stock market. Last month, we derisked the portfolio from the AI theme. June gave us a preview of why that was important. More on that later. Rebound Portfolio Performance Happy to report that the Rebound portfolio is now beating the market ( S&P 5… ## Key Claims - We have just crossed Rebound Capital’s 1st Anniversary , and I want to thank every one of you. - The fact that nearly 23,000 of you read my content is a big responsibility. - I will keep grinding and doing what I love - finding value in the stock market. - Last month, we derisked the portfolio from the AI theme. - June gave us a preview of why that was important. ## Evidence - We pair value with embedded catalysts - a discounted stock only interests us when the market is also materially underestimating where its earnings and key metrics are headed over the next 6 to 24 months. - The re-rating comes when the market is forced to upgrade its consensus estimates for those material KPIs. - Big tech will cut costs by designing custom compute (ASICs) and finding more efficient ways to use memory. - cut - Big tech will cut costs by designing custom compute (ASICs) and finding more efficient w - g tech will cut costs by designing custom compute (ASICs) and find - l cut costs by designing custom compute (ASICs) and find - A pause or a second look at capital expenditure on building out AI data centers may be around the corner. - This will shift more of the value in the AI stack towards cloud providers and away from frontier labs and semis. - The GLP-1 related headwinds are affecting this group as well (healthier people lead to lower need for medical devices). - The GLP-1 related headwinds ## Tensions _None flagged yet._ ## Links - Raw: `kb/inbox/c344b80ad07ba70e09bc71ca01268cc7550deae8e61c846aa15b30403c338286.json` - Concepts: [[concepts/13k|13k]] - Overview: [[overview]]
